The process removes elements at positions $1,4,7,\ldots$ (congruent to $1 \bmod 3$) in each round. If a list has $n$ elements, after one round it has $m = \lceil 2(n-1)/3 \rceil$ elements, and the element at new position $j$ came from original position $\lceil 3j/2\rceil$.

Let $g(n)$ be the surviving value (which equals its position since the list starts as $1,2,\ldots,n$). Then $g(1)=1$ and for $n\ge 2$:
$$g(n) = \left\lceil \tfrac32\, g\!\left(\lceil \tfrac{2(n-1)}{3}\rceil\right) \right\rceil.$$

Iterating this reduction for $n=2002$:
$$2002 \to 1334 \to 889 \to 592 \to 394 \to 262 \to 174 \to 116 \to 77 \to 51 \to 34 \to 22 \to 14 \to 9 \to 6 \to 4 \to 2 \to 1,$$
which takes 17 steps. Working backwards from $g(1)=1$ by repeatedly applying $x \mapsto \lceil 3x/2\rceil$ gives the sequence
$$1,\, 2,\, 3,\, 5,\, 8,\, 12,\, 18,\, 27,\, 41,\, 62,\, 93,\, 140,\, 210,\, 315,\, 473,\, 710,\, 1065,\, 1598.$$

Thus $g(2002) = 1598$.

\boxed{1598}
